backup.export-body: Save one file with every child's progress. Keep it somewhere safe.
backup.import-body: Pick a backup file from another device. Its progress merges with what's already here — nothing is lost.
backup.import-error-generic: This file could not be read.
backup.import-warning: Nothing is lost: both devices' progress is kept.
backup.share-body: Send every child's progress to the other device (AirDrop, Messages, Drive…). Nothing is lost: both devices' progress is kept.

parent.delete-confirm-body: This removes all saved progress for this child. This cannot be undone.

privacy.contact-body: Open an issue on the project's GitHub repository: {{url}}
privacy.control-body: Export or delete any child's data any time, from Backup and from that child's Settings in the parent area.
privacy.data-body: A nickname, an avatar picture, and lesson progress for each child — stored only on this device, never sent anywhere.
privacy.intro: {{app}} keeps everything on this device. Here's exactly what that means.
privacy.network-body: The only network access is checking for app updates. Updates are static files delivered from GitHub Pages. "Send to other device" hands the file to whichever app or device the parent picks — the app itself still sends nothing.
privacy.no-accounts-body: No sign-up, no analytics, no ads, no third-party services. The app never phones home.
privacy.title: Privacy

cls-boxes.demo: Is it red? Yes. Is it a circle? Yes. It goes where red meets circle.
cls-boxes.story: Pip sorts the shells into boxes. Each box has a rule. Check the card against the rule, then put it in.
cls-boxes.title: Two boxes

cls-circles.demo: Blue? Yes. A circle? No. It goes in the blue circle only.
cls-circles.story: Two circles, two rules. A card that fits both goes in the middle, where the circles meet. A card that fits neither stays outside.
cls-circles.title: Circles

cls-line-up.demo: Smallest first: tiny, then medium, then huge.
cls-line-up.story: Pip lines the shells up from smallest to biggest. Compare two at a time. If the bear is taller than the fox, and the fox is taller than the rabbit, then the bear is taller than the rabbit!
cls-line-up.title: Line up

cls-odd.demo: Three are circles. The square is the odd one out.
cls-odd.story: Pip found shells on the shore. They are all alike, except one! Check the colour, the shape, the size and how many.
cls-odd.title: Odd one out

cls-rule.demo: Different shapes, different sizes, but all red. They are all red!
cls-rule.story: Now Pip asks: what do they all share? Check one thing at a time: colour, then shape, then size.
cls-rule.title: Find the rule

grd-last.demo: This row has 1, 2 and 4. The missing number is 3.
grd-last.story: Pip has a number grid. The rule: each row, column and box has every number once. If only one cell is empty, which number is missing?
grd-last.title: Last empty cell

grd-only-number.demo: Its row has 1, its column has 2 and 4. Only 3 is left.
grd-only-number.story: Now pick one empty cell. Which numbers are already in its row, its column and its box? Cross them out. The number left is the answer.
grd-only-number.title: Only number

grd-only-place.demo: The 3s in these rows block two cells. Only one cell in the box can take the 3.
grd-only-place.story: Sometimes a number fits in only one place. Pick a box and a number. Cross out every cell that already sees that number. One cell is left!
grd-only-place.title: Only place

grd-pixels.demo: A 5 in a row of five: fill them all. A 0: cross them all out.
grd-pixels.story: Picture cross! The numbers say how many cells in a line are filled, in groups. Fill the cells you are sure of, cross out the empty ones, and a picture appears.
grd-pixels.title: Picture cross

grd-six.demo: This box already has 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. The empty cell gets 3.
grd-six.story: A bigger grid! Six numbers, and each box has two rows of three. The same tricks still work.
grd-six.title: Six by six

lessons.lu-order: The cat is bigger than the mouse. The dog is bigger than the cat. Put them in order, smallest first.
lessons.lu-shortest: The giraffe is taller than the horse. The horse is taller than the dog. Who is the shortest?
lessons.lu-tallest: The bear is taller than the fox. The fox is taller than the rabbit. Who is the tallest?
lessons.lu-true: The owl is taller than the hen. The hen is taller than the chick. True or false: the chick is taller than the owl.

pat-far.demo: Count in twos: numbers 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 are all blue. Number 10 is blue.
pat-far.story: Pip wants to know what comes much later. Count in whole parts that repeat, like red, blue. Red is always first in each part.
pat-far.title: Far ahead

pat-grow.demo: Each step has 2 more stars. 5 and 2 more make 7.
pat-grow.story: Some patterns grow. Count how many more there are each time. The next picture has that many more again.
pat-grow.title: Growing

pat-repeat.demo: Red circle, blue square, again and again. Next comes a blue square.
pat-repeat.story: Pip loves patterns. A pattern has a part that repeats, again and again. Find the part that repeats, then say what comes next!
pat-repeat.title: Repeat

pat-steps.demo: Every jump is plus 4. 15 plus 4 is 19.
pat-steps.story: Numbers can make patterns too. Look at the jump from one number to the next. Check every jump, not just the first one!
pat-steps.title: Number steps

pattern-train.goal: Every carriage follows the pattern. Which one comes next?
pattern-train.title: Pattern Train

sudoku-sprint.goal: Fill the grids, step by step!
sudoku-sprint.title: Sudoku Sprint
